sense.text:
The Bible is the playing field. The Israelites play from it, and the Christian church and the apologetics allegedly play from it too, so the question is who is lining up the precepts properly. It begins here: “The fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom”.

To fear God is to fear his judgments. The law says thou shalt not commit adultery, and the judgment for it is death, so a man is afraid of that. Christ died for sins, we have a chance of repentance and we are under grace, but grace is supposed to teach us to deny sin. Grace is not a license to sin.

“A good understanding have all they that do his commandments.” If you fear God and keep his commandments, that is how you become wise. The opposite is just as plain: if you are not keeping God’s commandments, you are not wise, and you will not have a good understanding of the scriptures.

So who understands the Bible? Show a scripture, Old or New Testament, of anyone who was not keeping the commandments and yet had the Holy Spirit, understood the Bible and taught it. It is not there. Everyone in the Bible who had understanding, prophet or teacher, kept the laws of God. The sacrificial law is done, the book of Hebrews explains that, but the moral laws stand. So how in 2025 do men believe they do not have to keep the laws and still claim to understand? Men sat and let a preacher spit in their hands and put the spit in their eyes, and passed it off as something godly. Why do they do that? Because they have no understanding. The Christian who still thinks he can eat pork is trying to put a circle in a square.

precepts.why:
“If thou desire wisdom, keep the commandments, and the Lord shall give her unto thee.” If you desire wisdom, the understanding of what God is explaining to us, you keep the commandments. You do not start looking for scriptures to explain why you do not have to keep the law.

Here is the prerequisite. God said he will give it to you, but here is the caveat: you have to keep the commandments. One preacher said that if you keep the commandments you are sinning, and the people sat there and said Praise Jesus. So God inspired these words, then got to the New Testament and threw it all out? That would make God bipolar, and God does not change. When Christ walked the earth there was no New Testament. What was he teaching from? What was Paul referencing?

And what is being fought over? We are telling men to stay home and raise your children, don’t be a deadbeat dad; telling women to stop wearing them pants when you walk out with camel toe and yeast infection. We are trying to help our people, and they are a hard-headed people who do not listen. That is why so many are sitting in prison: they refused to listen.

“For the fear of the Lord is wisdom and instruction: and faith and meekness are his delight.” The Lord wants you to have faith and a meek spirit, a pliable spirit. Before this truth, eating pork, shrimp, smoking weed and multiple women did not seem wrong; once the laws of God were learned, it was: I can’t do that no more. Do I love shrimp and crab more than God? Weed? Multiple women? A choice had to be made, and that is called repentance. That is being born again.

Old people refuse to change and say it does not matter, I’m under grace now, it’s what’s in the inner man. What is in the inner man is an evil man. That is in all of us; we were evil and we have to change. Meekness and faith is a spirit that understands: if I do these things, Lord, I am going to receive the kingdom, so I will humble down and change. The Lord said he will give wisdom, but keep my commandments. Show where that changed in the New Testament.

“If any of you lack wisdom, let him ask of God, that giveth to all men liberally, and upbraideth not; and it shall be given him.” It is the same thing read in Ecclesiasticus. The apologetics say the Israelites hopscotch around the Bible. Yes, we do. The Bible tells us to. The Christian church is good at semantic talk and catchy phrases, word soup: it sounds good, but it ain’t saying nothing, and the one who does not know better sits there befuddled and just goes with it.

It shall be given to you, but it begins with you: fear me and keep. God says, I will give you this, but I want obedience. They just want to say, I believe Jesus Christ is Lord, and that is all it takes. Can a wife tell her husband, I believe you’re my husband, and not do the things a husband dictates? That does not make sense. The whole Bible is a book of laws, and then in the New Testament they say we don’t have to keep the commandments.

“But let him ask in faith, nothing wavering.” The faith is this: if I abide by these commandments and do what you say, God, I will inherit the kingdom of heaven. Knowing that, we do not waver, and that is why we are bold in what we say. Some Israelite camps do not study; a brother who sits among us and studies six months would answer most of what the apologetics come with.

sense.text: “Jesus answered them, and said, My doctrine is not mine, but his that sent me.” Christ was sent. If a man said, I am God, I am the son and I am the spirit, and the father, me, sent me the son down here with me the spirit, the first thing you would do is see if he has Medicaid so he can see a therapist, and slowly back away: start the car.

“If any man will do his will, he shall know of the doctrine, whether it be of God, or whether I speak of myself.” If you are keeping his commandments and doing his will, you are going to understand the Bible and understand the doctrine.

The reason men could not understand Christ and his purpose is that they were open sinners, unrepentant. He was the one that was for to come, spoken of in Deuteronomy, the Psalms and the prophets, and they did not understand it, because they were not doing the will of God.
“He that speaketh of himself seeketh his own glory: but he that seeketh his glory that sent him, the same is true, and no unrighteousness is in him.” Christ sought the glory of the one that sent him.

precepts.why:
To prove the will of God, so no one can say it is made up: “I delight to do thy will, O my God: yea, thy law is within my heart.” The will of God is the laws of God. It is a law that is in your heart, and your heart is your mind. The laws of God are in your mind to do his will.

So if you know the will of God, you shall know the doctrine, whether it be of God. You do not know whether it is of God because you are not doing the will of God. It is like trying to fit a circle in a square. That is why, when they come to us, we overpower them: they do not understand basic things like you can’t eat pork, but they understand tithing. When you walk up on us we are in teacher mode, not debate mode. You are the student; we are the teacher.

And if someone says something above our learning, we keep quiet, take it in, and go search the scriptures to see whether those things are so. The white man plays a major part in this Bible too: somebody got to be the devil.

sense.text:
God is speaking to us in English. They say you have to go into the Greek to get the full understanding. But “the holy scriptures, which are able to make thee wise unto salvation”: the scriptures are what make you wise. If you want salvation, you better know these scriptures.

“Through faith which is in Christ Jesus.” The faith is that Jesus Christ came to die for his people, God’s people.

“All scripture is given by inspiration of God”. Christ said, Lo, I come in the volume of the book it is written of me, and there was no New Testament written then. All scripture is Old Testament and New Testament.

They say God did inspire the Old Testament but gave a new covenant, so we are no longer under the old. We know we are no longer under the sacrificial law; we no longer sacrifice. But they say the laws are done away with, and still they tithe: you can’t rob God. And the white image of Christ has been around so long, and nobody puts the same energy against that as they put against saying he is black.

It “is profitable for doctrine”, which is the laws of God, “for reproof, for correction, for instruction in righteousness”: to instruct you how to be righteous.
“That the man of God may be perfect, throughly furnished unto all good works.” All scripture is given for this.

precepts.why:
Where does it say Christ came to die for his people only? “But he answered and said, I am not sent but unto the lost sheep of the house of Israel.” He was sent, and not by himself. The word but means only: only for the lost sheep.

Christ, who died and rose from the dead, turned water into wine and fed a multitude with two fishes, would know what he came for and who he came for. How do you negate that? They will go to Revelation 7, all nations and kindreds and tongues, and to the writings of Paul. But you don’t understand Paul because you don’t understand Christ. Hopscotch anywhere in the Bible you want and give the precepts; we don’t run from it. It is not there.

sense.text:
“If ye fulfil the royal law according to the scripture, Thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself, ye do well”. This is what the Christians hold on to: love your neighbour, and you fulfil all the law.

But when Paul and James wrote these things as letters to the churches and to the brethren that were scattered, for what they said to be substantiated they had to draw from previous writings; otherwise it is just them talking. They needed a reference point, what we call today the Old Testament, to validate their sayings. That is why it says prove all things.

precepts.why:
“For all the law is fulfilled in one word, even in this; Thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself.” They read this and say: see, you fulfil the law if you love your neighbour; the law is fulfilled now, that’s it.

What they forgot is where Paul got that from. Go to the Old Testament and see what loving your neighbour means.

“Thou shalt not hate thy brother in thine heart: thou shalt in any wise rebuke thy neighbour, and not suffer sin upon him.” Loving your neighbour is teaching him. All scripture is given by inspiration of God and is profitable for reproof, for correction, for instruction in righteousness, so you have to teach him the laws of God: Hey bro, you know you’re breaking the law of God. You can’t do that. The law says this.

“Thou shalt not avenge, nor bear any grudge against the children of thy people, but thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself: I am the Lord.” This is what James was quoting. Do not hold a grudge, render not evil for evil, and do not suffer sin upon your brother: correct him. Ezekiel 3 says the same, or his blood is on your hand.

That Christianity stuff is a mirage. It is hocus pocus, it is witchcraft, and it destroys the minds of a people. People are confused because they do not keep the commandments.

sense.text:
When a man asks God for wisdom, God gives it, but he is not giving the wisdom of the world. He gives his wisdom for one purpose only. Some speak with fancy words that are not biblical, and people take that as wisdom, but God is not giving his wisdom to be used for deception.

“And I will give you pastors according to mine heart”, according to his mind, “which shall feed you with knowledge and understanding.” A man may sound intelligent, have a theology degree and doctor in front of his name; that is not the wisdom of God. The wisdom of God is to feed his sheep.

“In those days the house of Judah shall walk with the house of Israel”: the northern and southern kingdoms together. God gives wisdom to feed his sheep so that the house of Israel can come back as twelve tribes again.

It is not to save all nations, not to bring in other people, and not only to save Christians. The wisdom of God is given to gather the lost sheep of the house of Israel. If anybody sounds smart and sounds like he has wisdom, and he is not trying to gather the lost sheep of the house of Israel, that is the wisdom of the world.

“Go thy way, Daniel: for the words are closed up and sealed till the time of the end.” The word was to be sealed unto the end times. We are living in those end times, and the word is being unsealed right now. For them it is still sealed, because they do not understand.

The oxymoron is that Christianity has separated Christ from the commandments, and it is impossible to separate Christ from the commandments; they are one and the same. Christ is the word. When he left, he said, I will not leave you comfortless, and Lo, I come in the volume of the book: this is Christ in word form. He came in the flesh, went back to the Father, and gave us a new testament so we have no cloak for our sins. There were laws written because of the hardness of our hearts, like the law of divorcement, so he came and said, But I say unto you, for in the beginning it was not so. How do you separate Christ from the commandments, and then make Christ, the Holy Spirit and God one? You guys are crazy.

More important than any of us being right is that we be righteous. We pray they repent; this is not to make mockery of brothers who sincerely do not understand.

“The wicked shall do wickedly: and none of the wicked shall understand; but the wise shall understand.” The wicked are going to sin and will not understand, but the book is opened in the latter days and the wise shall understand. You are looking at the wise. It is not because of special theological studies at Yale or Harvard. It is because we get around men that are keeping his commandments, we learn, and God gives the increase. That is why IUIC does not run from any scripture.

If you are wise, you have wisdom; and if you desire wisdom, you have to keep the commandments. It keeps saying the same thing over and over.

“Evil men understand not judgment”. Judgment is the penalties for breaking the law, so evil men do not understand it because they do not know the law.

“But they that seek the Lord understand all things.” By process of elimination: if evil men do not understand judgment, the penalty for breaking the law, then seeking the Lord must be seeking his commandments. There would have to be a scripture explaining it.

precepts.why:
Asa “commanded Judah to seek the Lord God of their fathers, and to do the law and the commandment.” To seek the Lord is to do the law. Do is a verb, an action word.

Here come the Christians saying the law and the commandment are different. Shut your black lips. Nobody knows you are a fool if you keep quiet, and we were all fools once.

The laws and commandments are interchangeable: law, statutes and commandments. The law is the fullness of everything we are supposed to do, what is set in stone. The commandments are the moral things we are supposed to follow. The statutes are underneath them: the law says remember the sabbath day to keep it holy, and the statute is how you keep it holy: you don’t shop, you don’t cook. They all work together, one, the way we are one in Jesus and Jesus is one in God: all one, but all separate.

Seeking the Lord is doing the laws. “They that fear the Lord will not disobey his Word”, and his word is right here in the book. “And they that love him will keep his ways.” Christ said, if you love me, keep my commandments.

You would not go looking for precepts to explain why you don’t have to keep the laws. That is evil: you are seduced and you are a seducer. They call us the bad guys for keeping the laws and compelling God’s people to keep them. What was Daniel doing? Ezekiel? Jeremiah? Why was Christ killed? To bring people back to the laws of God. What was John the Baptist doing? Repent, for the kingdom of heaven is at hand.

“They that fear the Lord will seek that which is well pleasing unto him; and they that love him shall be filled with the law.” Isn’t that the same seeking the Lord read in Proverbs? Evil men understand not judgment, but they that seek the Lord understand. If you seek him, you will be filled with the law.

This sets the stage for showing why their doctrine is flawed: to get understanding, you have to keep the laws. An apologist would have to debunk every one of these scriptures.

“The knowledge of the commandments of the Lord is the doctrine of life: and they that do things that please him shall receive the fruit of the tree of immortality.” Do the things that please him and you receive the fruit of the tree of immortality. We want to live forever; we want that fruit.

“The fear of the Lord is all wisdom; and in all wisdom is the performance of the law, and the knowledge of his omnipotency.” The fear of the Lord is what makes you wise, and in all wisdom is doing the law and understanding how great and powerful he is: that God made his son Jesus Christ through his word, sent his word down, and his word leapt down from the throne, dwelt among men and died. And Christ did not leave us comfortless; he gave the New Testament for comfort, and the comfort found there is Revelation 13, verses 9 and 10.

“If a servant say to his master, I will not do as it pleaseth thee; though afterward he do it, he angereth him that nourisheth him.”

“The knowledge of wickedness is not wisdom”. That goes back to Jeremiah 3:15: God is not giving his wisdom for wickedness. Many in this world take the knowledge of wickedness to disobey the laws and call it wisdom. That is handling the word of God deceitfully, teaching a people they don’t have to keep the laws of God. He that breaketh the least commandment and teaches men so shall be called least in the kingdom, and least does not mean a regular guy in the kingdom; it means punished. There will be no least of the righteous in the kingdom; we will all shine.

“Neither at any time the counsel of sinners prudence.” A man telling you that you don’t got to keep the commandments is a sinner, and it is not prudent to listen to him. Not prudent to listen to one who says if you don’t pay tithe we’ll shoot you down in the church, when tithing was grain and the first of your flocks. Not prudent when the pastor preaching to you, his first lady is a man.

“And they that remain shall know that there is nothing better than the fear of the Lord, and that there is nothing sweeter than to take heed unto the commandments of the Lord.” What stands out is “they that remain.” Remain from what? Go back up in the chapter.

“This man shall be punished in the streets of the city, and where he suspecteth not he shall be taken.” They that remain are those not punished. Then of the woman: “For first, she hath disobeyed the law of the most High; and secondly, she hath trespassed against her own husband; and thirdly, she hath played the whore in adultery, and brought children by another man.” She is breaking the commandments. “She shall be brought out into the congregation, and inquisition shall be made of her children. Her children shall not take root, and her branches shall bring forth no fruit. She shall leave her memory to be cursed, and her reproach shall not be blotted out.” Why? Because she sinned against God. And they say the laws don’t matter no more? Christ told the woman taken in adultery to sin no more.

So they that remain are those that learn not to sin against God, and they learn there is nothing better than the fear of the Lord. The fear of God is the beginning of wisdom, and wisdom teaches that there is a punishment for breaking the laws of God. They say we are under grace, but grace is supposed to teach you to deny ungodliness. God forbid that we continue in sin that grace may abound; we establish the law.

There is nothing sweeter than taking heed to the commandments of the Lord. The fruit of eternal life is sweet. An hour has gone by speaking of nothing but getting understanding and avoiding sin, and they will dismiss all of it and say we don’t have to keep the laws of God. Then you don’t understand the Bible.

sense.text: Now the New Testament. “For when ye were the servants of sin, ye were free from righteousness.” When you were serving sin, you were let loose from being righteous. It is one or the other: a servant to sin cannot be righteous.

“What fruit had ye then in those things whereof ye are now ashamed?” You should be ashamed of the sinner you were. What was the fruit of smoking weed? Cancer. Of whoredom, AIDS. Of eating pork, gout and high blood pressure. “For the end of those things is death.”

“But now being made free from sin, and become servants to God, ye have your fruit unto holiness, and the end everlasting life.” There is nothing sweeter than that.

What is being brought out is that these apologetics are actually teaching sin. Notice they never have a video about improving a nation, improving our people, who are in a lost, destroyed state. They have no solutions. They are at our heels like dogs chasing a car, trying to stop what God has ordained, and you cannot stop it.

“For the wages of sin is death”. Sin is the transgression of the law, and its wages are death, not eternal life. “But the gift of God is eternal life through Jesus Christ our Lord.” Eternal life is through Christ, and Christ said, if you love me, keep my commandments. What scripture will they give for obtaining eternal life another way?
If eternal life is through Jesus Christ, then do this: “Let not sin therefore reign in your mortal body, that ye should obey it in the lusts thereof.”

“Neither yield ye your members as instruments of unrighteousness unto sin: but yield yourselves unto God”. Do not yield yourself unto sin; yield your members “as instruments of righteousness unto God.” Apply righteousness in your life.

“For sin shall not have dominion over you: for ye are not under the law, but under grace.” Here they say: there you go, you’re not under the law. But after saying let not sin reign in your mortal body, would Paul now say we don’t have to keep the laws? That would make Paul, inspired by God, bipolar.

Sin shall not have dominion over you because you do not yield yourself unto unrighteousness and do not let sin reign in your mortal body. And you are not under the law because you no longer have to give up sacrificial turtledoves and bulls and rams. That is the law. But you are under grace. That is not our own breakdown: God has to explain what he means, and he does.

precepts.why: In the same chapter, verse one: “What shall we say then? Shall we continue in sin, that grace may abound? God forbid. How shall we, that are dead to sin, live any longer therein?” Read with that, not under the law cannot mean free to sin. It would not make sense.

What law are we no longer under? Stay in the New Testament, because they would say, see, you’re going to the Old Testament, we’re under the new covenant. Luke shows it: “to offer a sacrifice according to that which is said in the law of the Lord, A pair of turtledoves, or two young pigeons.”

We are no longer under that law. The law Paul is talking about is the law of sacrifice, the turtledoves. We don’t have to leave the New Testament to show it.

And what is grace? “For the grace of God that bringeth salvation hath appeared to all men, Teaching us that, denying ungodliness and worldly lusts”. Grace teaches us to deny being ungodly: don’t let sin reign in your mortal bodies, because the wages of sin is death; don’t yield yourself to obey the lusts thereof.

“We should live soberly”: sober minded, not tossed to and fro, wavering with every wind of doctrine, as James said. “Righteously, and godly, in this present world”: the present time, the present day. Things written aforetime were written for our learning.

To all of our people: the commandments are key in salvation and the commandments are key in understanding. One of them said, show me in the New Testament where you have to wear fringes, where you have to grow a beard. Christ, his apostles and Paul taught from what we call the Old Testament and brought people to repentance with it. Saying the New Testament supersedes it, you are speaking an idle word and are in danger of the judgment of God. Take a pen and paper out; you need to be retaught.

sense.text: “Therefore seeing we have this ministry, as we have received mercy, we faint not”: we do not faint in this truth.

“But have renounced the hidden things of dishonesty, not walking in craftiness, nor handling the word of God deceitfully”. Not walking in craftiness means our speech is plain speech. We are talking to the average brother out there on the corner. Black men don’t talk about exegesis and eisegesis and Hebrew Israelism and legalism. That is old church foolishness to make you sound deep. The average brother in the street is asking, why are we getting beat over our head? Why are we going through this? Because we sinned against God. The wisdom of the world is foolishness with him. That does not work on us.

“But by manifestation of the truth commending ourselves to every man’s conscience in the sight of God.”

“But if our gospel be hid, it is hid to them that are lost”. If the gospel is not hid to you, you understand, and if you understand, you are keeping the commandments. If the gospel is hid to you, you don’t understand, and that is because you are lost in sin.

precepts.why:
Handling the word of God deceitfully: “Cursed be he that doeth the work of the Lord deceitfully, and cursed be he that keepeth back his sword from blood.” Talk plain to black people; we are a plain people and we need plain words.

They don’t want to see the white man go into captivity. They are trying to hold that back, trying to save their master. But we are going to read the scriptures and show it, like it or not: he is going to get it along with the other nations. Yes, he plays a big part. Esau and Jacob is all over the Bible; read Obadiah. God had enemies, and the Israelites had enemies.

Saying all nations can be saved is handling this word deceitfully. Christ said, I am not sent but unto the lost sheep of the house of Israel. Will you stand before the Messiah in that day and tell him he didn’t mean that? He had the scribes, he had the book published, he inspired men of God to write it, he told John, write down what you see. Off with your head.

This is Christ speaking: “He that believeth on me, as the scripture hath said”. Believe on him as it is written. Don’t give exegesis, eisegesis, Hebrewism or hermeneutics. Just believe what is written, in plain speech.

“So they read in the book in the law of God distinctly, and gave the sense, and caused them to understand the reading.” They gave the sense of what was being said. Don’t try to be deep with all the semantics. They caused the people to understand, and to understand you have to keep the commandments.

This one is for the dumb apologetics. It is what was just read in Nehemiah 8:8: they gave the sense and caused them to understand. “And my speech and my preaching was not with enticing words of man’s wisdom”. That is what the apologetics do. They use enticing words: hermeneutics, eisegesis, essence, finite and local, condescending, knowing full well that when black people hear condescending they don’t think, he humbled himself. You know it is man’s wisdom by its fruit.

Paul said he came “in demonstration of the Spirit and of power.” The Spirit and the power are in keeping God’s commandments. Drug dealers on the corner hear, you are supposed to love your neighbour as yourself, you can’t be a murderer, and they say, dang, let me change that. They are not changed by somebody saying that ain’t the right hermeneutics. That is why Nehemiah 8:8 says what it says: give them the sense, so they understand what they read. Our people ain’t understanding when you eisegete and exegete.

Is there a scripture that says the gospel is hid to the lost because of sin? “I brought you up with gladness; but with sorrow and heaviness have I lost you: for ye have sinned before the Lord your God, and done that thing that is evil before him.” The gospel is hid to them that have sinned. That is why they don’t understand it: they are lost.

If you break the commandments and teach men so, you shall be called least in the kingdom of heaven. You have done evil before God and handled the word of God deceitfully. You told the people Christ died for everyone, and he said, I am not sent but unto the lost sheep of the house of Israel. But God so loved the world? You are lost. You do not have a good understanding of what it means, because you are not keeping the commandments.

sense.text:
“And I saw another angel fly in the midst of heaven, having the everlasting gospel to preach unto them that dwell on the earth, and to every nation, and kindred, and tongue, and people”. They thought we would run from this scripture. We don’t. They hopscotch, but they won’t hop on the scriptures that are hot; they dance around them with their hermeneutics.

Every nation, every kindred, every tongue, every people: it sounds like everybody on the earth, and not knowing the Bible, that is what anyone would say. Revelation says the same thing in chapter 7, and the precepts show who that multitude out of every nation is: the children of Israel, scattered into every nation.

“After this I beheld, and, lo, a great multitude, which no man could number, of all nations, and kindreds, and people, and tongues, stood before the throne, and before the Lamb, clothed with white robes, and palms in their hands”. It appears to be talking about all nations, tongues and people.

But the people that could not be numbered are the children of Israel. And it says of all nations and kindreds and tongues because Israel was scattered throughout all of them. These are the devout Jews, that no man can number, coming from all over the earth.

precepts.why:
This is why we hopscotch: God told us to. “Whom shall he teach knowledge?” Knowledge is the law; the priest’s lips should keep knowledge, and they should seek the law at his mouth. “And whom shall he make to understand doctrine?” Doctrine is the law of God.

“Them that are weaned from the milk, and drawn from the breasts.” They learn the deep basics, the laws of God, found primarily in the beginning of the Bible: thou shalt not commit adultery, thou shalt not murder, thou shalt not steal. That is the milk, when you are a baby on the breast. When you have had all that milk, then you can go to Revelation and understand what he is talking about.

“For precept must be upon precept, precept upon precept; line upon line, line upon line; here a little, and there a little”. That is how the Bible is meant to be read. It is not written in chronological order, because he did not want to reveal it to everybody, but to his servants the prophets.

There happens to be a scripture in the Bible that explains it: “I Esdras saw upon the mount Sion a great people, whom I could not number, and they all praised the Lord with songs.” Ezra saw the same thing John saw: a great people he could not number, all praising the Lord.

For this to be substantiated there would have to be an Old Testament scripture, the Old Testament they say doesn’t really matter. That is why their understanding is incomplete and flawed.

“Yet the number of the children of Israel shall be as the sand of the sea, which cannot be measured nor numbered”. The people of that day understood, because God unsealed the book to them while they kept the commandments: the number that could not be numbered was the children of Israel.

But why does it say all nations and kindreds and people? Because Israel was scattered throughout. “And the Lord shall scatter you among the nations, and ye shall be left few in number among the heathen, whither the Lord shall lead you.”

“And the Lord shall scatter thee among all people”: nations, people and kindred, “from the one end of the earth even unto the other; and there thou shalt serve other gods, which neither thou nor thy fathers have known, even wood and stone.”

“I said, I would scatter them into corners, I would make the remembrance of them to cease from among men”. Three scriptures explaining that the Israelites were going to be scattered. But they will say that was the Old Testament and we are under the new covenant, so go to Acts 2.

“And there were dwelling at Jerusalem Jews, devout men, out of every nation under heaven.” They were out of every nation because they were scattered, as God said in Deuteronomy 4, Deuteronomy 28 and Deuteronomy 32, and in Isaiah 11, Ezekiel 37, 1 Peter 1 and James 1.

“Every man heard them speak in his own language”: out of every tongue. “And how hear we every man in our own tongue, wherein we were born?” Parthians and Medes and the rest: these were devout Jews, born in the lands they were scattered into, come back to Jerusalem for the feast of Pentecost.

There would have to be some record written that these Jews were going to come back, and who would understand it? Those keeping the commandments would understand that they would be coming back.

“The Lord shall set his hand again the second time to recover the remnant of his people, which shall be left, from Assyria, and from Egypt, and from Pathros, and from Cush, and from Elam”, and from the islands of the sea. He is going to recover them back again.

“And he shall set up an ensign for the nations”, because we are scattered into all lands, “and shall assemble the outcasts of Israel, and gather together the dispersed of Judah”. That is what we read in Acts 2, and what is spoken of in Revelation 7: devout Jews, that no man can number, coming from all over the earth.

sense.text:
A Christian on video says he believes there is one God in three different distinct personalities, and when asked to explain, says God’s ways are higher than our ways and our minds cannot comprehend him. That is their camp 101. When you go into God’s ways are higher than our ways, you open the floodgates, and any doctrine can come in. God has principles he lives by, and one of them is not schizophrenia: God cannot lie. You can’t make a Marvel universe with a Spider-Man here and a Miles Morales over there. That is not how God works.

“For God is not the author of confusion, but of peace, as in all churches of the saints.” Three in one, three distinct, and distinct means totally different, yet one: that is confusion. God said if you want understanding, keep my commandments. It is easy to understand. He gave straight commandments.

And see what spiritual eyes see in that video: a man with his head covered, women in the audience with heads uncovered, and nobody corrected it. That is New Testament, 1 Corinthians. How can God inhabit that place and move them to understand the Bible while they break the commandments right then? Christ said, if you love me, keep my commandments.
This is the scripture they use for the trinity. “Whosoever believeth that Jesus is the Christ is born of God”. Jesus the Christ is born of God: how is he born of himself?

“For this is the love of God, that we keep his commandments: and his commandments are not grievous.” We are not grieving keeping God’s laws. It is not hard to not eat pork, shrimp and crab, not murder, not steal, not commit adultery. It is not hard for women not to wear pants, for men not to wear dresses, not to be gay. Why are they fighting us over women not wearing pants? Because they are evil.

“And this is the victory that overcometh the world, even our faith.” Our faith is the victory, because we believe. “Who is he that overcometh the world, but he that believeth that Jesus is the Son of God?” The people did not believe that Jesus was the Son of God. If Jesus is the Son of God, how can he be the Father?

“This is he that came by water and blood, even Jesus Christ”. He came in the fleshly form, compacted in blood and water.

“Not by water only”: the water is the word. He did not come to us only in the word. That is why he said, Lo, I come in the volume of the book. He came in the flesh, he was with us in the word, he was with us in the wilderness in the cloud, and he will be with us in the end as the comforter. This Bible has layers.

“And it is the Spirit that beareth witness, because the Spirit is truth.” The spirit is the word, and the word bears truth that he is the Son of God, the Messiah that was for to come. All through the Old Testament, Isaiah 53 and many places, explains it.

“For there are three that bear record in heaven, the Father, the Word, and the Holy Ghost: and these three are one.” Three bear record in heaven that he is the Son of God: the Father, the Word that leapt down, and the Holy Ghost. They say these three are one entity. No: one as Christ and the Father are one, one accord, as the people gathered themselves together as one man.

The word trinity is not even in the Bible. The doctrine did not exist in the Bible and was not taught by Christ, the apostles or Israel. It was made up over 250 years after Christ, through political councils, the council of Nicaea and the council of Constantinople, in 325 and 381. The word was begun by Tertullian around 200 AD. Many did not believe it and were put out, because they were mixing pagan customs into Christianity. That whole concept of a trinity goes back to Nimrod. Go and research it yourself.

So if someone runs up and asks, do you believe in the trinity? Where did you get that from? It is not in the Bible, and you are supposed to speak the word of God. Israelites who are unlearned get trapped, and some break off into stepchild orphan camps, pygmy camps, call themselves bishops and deacons after two years, and start saying all nations can be saved.

“And there are three that bear witness in earth, the spirit”, which is the word, “and the water”, which is the word, “and the blood”, which is Christ: “and these three agree in one.” They all agree in one. It is saying the same thing again: the spirit bears record that Christ is the Messiah.

precepts.why: How do we know came by water and blood means that? “But when they came to Jesus, and saw that he was dead already, they brake not his legs: But one of the soldiers with a spear pierced his side, and forthwith came there out blood and water.” That shows he came in the fleshly form.
When did he come to us by water? “That he might sanctify and cleanse it with the washing of water by the word”. The washing of water is by the word.

“In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God”. The word is synonymous with water. He did not come to us by the word only; he came by water and blood. That is why he said, Lo, I come in the volume of the book.

The Father bears record in heaven: “behold a voice out of the cloud, which said, This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased; hear ye him.” If Christ were the Father, it would say, this is me, in whom I am well pleased, hear me. The Lord is not the author of confusion.

The Word bears record in heaven, and the Word is Christ, who came from heaven: “Thine Almighty word leaped down from heaven out of thy royal throne, as a fierce man of war into the midst of a land of destruction”. The word came down from heaven and testified. The Bible defines itself.

The Holy Ghost bears record in heaven: “them that have preached the gospel unto you with the Holy Ghost sent down from heaven”. The Holy Spirit was sent down from heaven. These are the three that bear record in heaven: the Father, the Word and the Holy Spirit.

And these three are one. They say that means one entity. Christ says to the Father: “Holy Father, keep through thine own name those whom thou hast given me, that they may be one, as we are.” There are many of us here, but we are all one: one mind, one mission, to raise up the twelve tribes of Israel. Jesus is on the same accord with God, and asks that those God gave him be on the same accord with them.

For the thought that many can be one to be substantiated, there would have to be an Old Testament scripture to validate it. These men were experts in the law; they would have asked, where did you make this up from? That is what we ask of the trinity, because that ain’t Bible.

“And when the seventh month was come, and the children of Israel were in the cities, the people gathered themselves together as one man”. This is a nation of people coming together and moving as one man. Are they one man? Stop the hermeneutics. Now it makes sense: these three are one the way Israel gathered as one man.

The spirit bears record that Christ is the Messiah. “And they said, Some say that thou art John the Baptist: some, Elias; and others, Jeremias, or one of the prophets. He saith unto them, But whom say ye that I am? And Simon Peter answered and said, Thou art the Christ, the Son of the living God.” The Son of himself?

“Blessed art thou, Simon Bar–jona: for flesh and blood hath not revealed it unto thee, but my Father which is in heaven.” Man did not show Peter this. The Father in heaven put this spirit on him, and it bears witness that Christ is.

“Upon this rock I will build my church”. That church is being built right now under Christ, because we are speaking the word of God. As much as they shadowban us and refuse us interviews, they can’t stop the movement. We are on ground level, gathering the young, while the churches gather old people, and the young ones in there are effeminate and weak. We are not going to eisegete you to death; we are going to give you the word of God and show you what it means.

“But there is a spirit in man: and the inspiration of the Almighty giveth them understanding.” God inspires and gives understanding to them that keep the commandments. The inspiration of God is on them. That is why we don’t run from these scriptures: whatever they talk about, we will answer it.

sense.text: “The Ancient of days did sit, whose garment was white as snow, and the hair of his head like the pure wool”. The Ancient of days is the most high God, the one Christ answers to. The head of Christ is God.

The beast was slain and his body given to the burning flame. “As concerning the rest of the beasts, they had their dominion taken away: yet their lives were prolonged for a season and time.” They lost their dominion, but their lives were prolonged for a season.

This is what Daniel saw in a vision: “one like the Son of man came with the clouds of heaven, and came to the Ancient of days, and they brought him near before him.” The Ancient of days was there, and the Son of man came to him. What are you people smoking, to make them one?

precepts.why:
Now the New Testament. “But every man in his own order: Christ the firstfruits; afterward they that are Christ’s at his coming.” For there to be first fruits, there has to be a tree already. Christ is the first fruit, and after came us.

“Then cometh the end, when he shall have delivered up the kingdom to God, even the Father”. That is what was just read in Daniel 7: Christ coming to the Ancient of days, his Father, and delivering the kingdom to him. “For he must reign, till he hath put all enemies under his feet.” God has enemies, Christ has enemies, and we are with Christ, his fruits afterwards, so we have enemies. “The last enemy that shall be destroyed is death”, because Christ has the keys of hell and death.

“It is manifest that he is excepted, which did put all things under him. And when all things shall be subdued unto him, then shall the Son also himself be subject unto him that put all things under him”. When all nations are destroyed and Christ is reigning, he is going to put everything under God his Father. That was his mission: to do the will of his Father. Old Testament and New Testament say the same thing. So how can that be him? The Lord is not the author of confusion.

To the other Israelite camps: don’t let these men run up on you with this. You have to study, and teach more than that the white man is a devil. Even though he is, the Bible is far bigger than that, and it is not the crux of what we are here for. Our job is to raise up the twelve tribes of Israel. We live at peace with all men; we are not trying to rob or harm anyone. We are a nonviolent, Bible-based people; our job is to teach our people.

sense.text:
An apologist says Revelation 1:14-16 does not describe Jesus’ ethnicity: it is a symbolic apocalyptic vision of the glorified Christ, revealing his divinity, not a studio portrait. First, it does not reveal his ethnicity; it reveals his color. And Christ is the one who said to write it down: “What thou seest, write in a book, and send it unto the seven churches which are in Asia”.

John was in prison. Christ told him, I need you to write down what you see, write down my image, and send it to the churches. Did John not know what he looked like before? And it is more than his color: it is the fall of Esau. At the end of Revelation is the fall of the white man, and it is written in that form because he did not want everybody to understand it, the same way he spoke to the apostles in parables, and because they read your letters in jail. Send it to the churches about the mark of the beast, the twelve gates and the twelve tribes of Israel, because it is going to be unsealed in the last days, by those keeping the commandments. He will give them understanding and they will explain these things.

He says we have an identity crisis. Yes, we do: Christ white is a lie, the Jews being white is counterfeit, and they took our identity from us. Read Jeremiah 17:4: we shall be discontinued. It was not our idea to put his color in the book. And he says Daniel 7:9 points out eternal wisdom. No: we read that the Ancient of days sat, and the Son of man came to him, his Father. The Ancient of days is not Christ.

He says the feet like fine brass mean strength and endurance, that it is almost impossible to melt bronze no matter what heat you apply. Brass and bronze start melting around 1,600 degrees, and compared with other metals they melt at moderate temperatures. Fools hate knowledge. He wants so badly to save everybody else that he hates to believe Christ is a man of color. We pray he receives it; we are not making mockery of him, but of his breakdown.

precepts.why: “For what if some did not believe? shall their unbelief make the faith of God without effect? God forbid: yea, let God be true, but every man a liar”. Let the Bible be true: he said he was black with woolly hair. Explaining that away as bronze meaning strength and endurance makes you a liar. Come out of those churches.

sense.text: An apologist on video uses Deuteronomy 29 to say the Gentiles were included in the covenant. Stay right where he went, and since they say we take things out of context, read from verse one: “These are the words of the covenant, which the Lord commanded Moses to make with the children of Israel in the land of Moab, beside the covenant which he made with them in Horeb.” God commanded Moses to make this covenant with the children of Israel.
“Keep therefore the words of this covenant, and do them, that ye may prosper in all that ye do.” Who is the ye? Israel. Israel may prosper.

“Ye stand this day all of you before the Lord your God”. Who is the God of Israel? He is the God of Israel and none else. “Your captains of your tribes, your elders, and your officers, with all the men of Israel”: all Israelites.

“Your little ones, your wives, and thy stranger that is in thy camp, from the hewer of thy wood unto the drawer of thy water”. The strangers are not Israelites; they are the other nations within the camp, our servants, hewing wood and drawing water. They were there, and they had to keep the commandments, but the covenant was not with them.

“That thou shouldest enter into covenant with the Lord thy God, and into his oath”, “That he may establish thee to day for a people unto himself, and that he may be unto thee a God, as he hath said unto thee, and as he hath sworn unto thy fathers, to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob.”

“Neither with you only do I make this covenant and this oath; But with him that standeth here with us this day before the Lord our God, and also with him that is not here with us this day”: with Israel in the last days. He did not read this far, so we read it all, so no one can say it was taken out of context.

precepts.why:
Who were the strangers with us? Go to the next book, Joshua, who was around the same time as Moses. “Then Joshua built an altar unto the Lord God of Israel in mount Ebal”, and “he wrote there upon the stones a copy of the law of Moses, which he wrote in the presence of the children of Israel.”

“And all Israel, and their elders, and officers, and their judges, stood on this side the ark and on that side before the priests the Levites, which bare the ark of the covenant of the Lord, as well the stranger, as he that was born among them”. The hewers of wood and drawers of water were among us; when we came out of Egypt we had a mixed multitude of other nations with us.

“Half of them over against mount Gerizim”, where the blessings went up, “and half of them over against mount Ebal”, where the curses were set, “that they should bless the people of Israel.” They were with us, but they were not getting the blessings with us. Somebody got to do the work.

“There was not a word of all that Moses commanded, which Joshua read not before all the congregation of Israel, with the women, and the little ones, and the strangers that were conversant among them.” They were conversant: they knew the laws, they had to be circumcised, they had to keep the sabbath. But were they getting the blessings with us?

Brothers who don’t study and don’t keep the commandments don’t have a good understanding of this, and these men trap them. The apologetics study because the false teaching that all nations can be saved is in their mind, so they stretch and pull, but they do not rightly divide the word.

sense.text:
An Israelite on video shows from Deuteronomy 28 that our people were scattered in ships through the earth, and the Christian answers that he has three primary sources showing it was literally fulfilled by actual Jews before the transatlantic slave trade. The first primary source is the Bible, and the Bible doesn’t need a mate. His primary sources supersede the word of God.

“Seek ye out of the book of the Lord, and read”: prove what you have to prove in the book of the Lord. “No one of these shall fail”: none of these prophecies are going to fail. They say Deuteronomy is not even a prophetic book; and it shall come to pass is not prophetic? “None shall want her mate”: none of these prophecies needs a secondary source. God answers his own words in his word. Anything else we use is a secondary source, never the primary source.

And his own kind of source shows the opposite: a book on the Jews and Moors in Spain tells how, in the 1400s, Jewish children were torn from their parents, baptized and given to Christians to be raised, as slaves, and others were put on board ships. He said it was fulfilled at the time of Titus, in 70 AD; this is the 1400s. Deuteronomy 28:68 is what it is.

A Christian on video says John was writing to people influenced by Gnosticism, so keeping his word is not keeping the law. Make the word plain. Gnosticism holds that the material world is flawed and evil; this world is flawed and evil. That salvation comes through secret knowledge from a divine messenger; this is not for everybody to understand. That it awakens humanity to escape the material prison; that is what is happening right now, and we are not caught up in this world. Christ is a saviour, but the point of what they call Gnosticism is to come out of the world and stop following the things of the world.

“The earth is given into the hand of the wicked: he covereth the faces of the judges thereof; if not, where, and who is he?” Whoever is the wickedest covered the faces and changed the image of Christ and the apostles. We know who it is.

precepts.why:
“Then was Jesus led up of the Spirit into the wilderness to be tempted of the devil.” The devil tempted him with bread and with the pinnacle of the temple, and Christ answered, “It is written, Man shall not live by bread alone, but by every word that proceedeth out of the mouth of God”, and “Thou shalt not tempt the Lord thy God.”

“Again, the devil taketh him up into an exceeding high mountain, and sheweth him all the kingdoms of the world, and the glory of them; And saith unto him, All these things will I give thee, if thou wilt fall down and worship me.” For the devil to give it, it has to be in his hand. The earth is given into the hand of the wicked. So to deny the world and the evil of this world: what is wrong with that?

sense.text:
They say Gnosticism is salvation through secret knowledge imparted by a divine messenger. The divine messenger is Christ. “Why speakest thou unto them in parables? He answered and said unto them, Because it is given unto you to know the mysteries of the kingdom of heaven, but to them it is not given.” Christ said that.

Here is the point behind everything: the beginning of understanding is keeping God’s commandments. Without keeping God’s commandments you will not understand this Bible, and that goes for all of us. We pray the apologetics repent, sit down and study. We must adhere, repent and keep the commandments.

precepts.why: “And with many such parables spake he the word unto them, as they were able to hear it. But without a parable spake he not unto them: and when they were alone, he expounded all things to his disciples.” He expounded it to his disciples separately. The knowledge is not given to everybody.
